record.original_question: For an open dynamical system with a hole H ⊂ Ω, survival probability P(t), escape rate γ = - lim_{t→∞} (1/t) ln P(t), and natural invariant measure ν on the repeller, for which classes of maps and flows does the escape-rate formula γ = ∑_{i:λ_i>0} λ_i - h_KS remain valid, where the sum runs over positive Lyapunov exponents and h_KS is the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy computed with respect to ν?

evidence.quote: Pesin’s formula generalises in the open case to the “escape rate formula” [28, 37] γ = ∑ i:λi>0 λi − hKS (6) where the quantities on the right hand side are defined with respect to ν.

The escape rate formula has very recently been shown for a system that is not uniformly hyperbolic [12], however there is wide scope for further development both in maps without uniform hyperbolicity and in flows. Open problem 1. How general is the escape rate formula, Eq. (6)?

artifact.category_tag: escape rate formula in open dynamical systems
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Omega, T)$ be a discrete-time dynamical system (or, alternatively, a smooth flow) on a Riemannian manifold $\Omega$, and let $H \subset \Omega$ be a measurable subset (the "hole"). Define the survival set up to time $t$ as the set of points whose orbit up to time $t$ never enters $H$, and let $P(t)$ denote the Lebesgue (or a fixed reference) measure of this set, called the survival probability. Define the escape rate by
$$\gamma = -\lim_{t\to\infty} \frac{1}{t}\ln P(t),$$
assuming the limit exists. Suppose there exists a natural conditionally invariant probability measure $\nu$ supported on the repeller (the set of points that never escape under either forward or backward iteration). Let $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_d$ denote the Lyapunov exponents of $T$ with respect to $\nu$, and let $h_{KS}(\nu)$ denote the Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy of $T$ with respect to $\nu$.

Determine the broadest classes of maps and flows (in particular beyond the uniformly hyperbolic setting, including non-uniformly hyperbolic maps and continuous-time flows) for which the escape rate formula
$$\gamma = \sum_{i:\, \lambda_i > 0} \lambda_i - h_{KS}(\nu)$$
holds. Specifically, identify hypotheses on $T$, $H$, and $\nu$ under which this identity remains valid.
artifact.status_search_result: The escape rate formula is classical for uniformly hyperbolic open systems and has been extended in special non-uniformly hyperbolic cases, but a general characterization across non-uniformly hyperbolic maps and flows has not been established. Surveys on non-uniform hyperbolicity list related questions (e.g., Eckmann–Ruelle-type conjectures) as still open in full generality, supporting the view that the question of how general the escape rate formula is remains open.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in the Theory of Non-Uniform Hyperbolicity
status_evidence.snippet: Collection of open problems in non-uniformly hyperbolic dynamics, including questions on entropy and Lyapunov exponents.
status_evidence.claim: Generalizations of Pesin-type formulas beyond uniform hyperbolicity remain active open problems.

status_evidence.title: A note on Eckmann–Ruelle's conjecture (arXiv:1508.01313)
status_evidence.snippet: The Eckmann–Ruelle conjecture has been proved for uniformly partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms, Julia sets of rational maps, certain billiards and open systems.
status_evidence.claim: Related entropy/Lyapunov identities are known only for restricted classes, with the general case open.

status_evidence.title: Pesin theory - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Pesin's entropy formula relates Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy to positive Lyapunov exponents under absolute continuity assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: The closed-system Pesin formula is the prototype that the open-system escape rate formula generalizes.
